questions.question: How did missionary scholars contribute to the growth of Malayalam prose?
questions.solution_html:
• Missionary scholars played a crucial role in the development and growth of Malayalam
  • prose, especially during the 19th century. Missionaries established schools and promoted
  • mass education. They started early Malayalam journals and magazines. They established
  • some of the earliest printing pr esses in Kerala, which made it possible to produce books,
  • pamphlets, and periodicals in Malayalam. This helped standardize written prose and
  • increased its reach.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: How did LMS missionaries contribute to the spread of English education in Kerala?
questions.solution_html:
• LMS missionaries founded many schools where English was taught along with Malayalam.
  • These ins titutions provided access to modern education, especially in regions like South
  • Kerala. They introduced subjects such as science, mathematics, and history, all taught
  • through English.

questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Describe the significance of the Basel Mission Press at Thalassery under Dr. Gundert’s leadership.
questions.solution_html:
• The Basel Mission Press at Thalassery, under the leadership of Hermann Gundert, played a
  • vital role in the devel opment of Malayalam language, literature, and journalism. Under
  • Gundert’s guidance, the press became one of the most important centres for printing in
  • Kerala. It produced books, textbooks, and periodicals in Malayalam, making printed
  • materials widely available.

questions.question: Discuss the contribution of nationalist newspapers in Kerala’s political awakening.
questions.solution_html:
• Nationalist newspapers played a crucial role in Kerala’s political awakening during the late
  • 19th and early 20th centuries. They acted as powerful tools for spreading political ideas,
  • mobilizing publ ic opinion, and resisting colonial rule. Newspapers such as
  • Swadeshabhimani and Kesari promoted the ideals of freedom, self -rule (Swaraj), and
  • national unity. They helped people understand the goals of the Indian national movement.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the significance of Mangalam in the growth of commercial journalism in Kerala.
questions.solution_html:
• Mangalam played a significant role in the growth of commercial journalism in Kerala ,
  • especially from the late 20th century onward. Mangalam shifted focus from purely political
  • or literary journalism to people-centric and entertainment -oriented content . It included
  • cinema news, human-interest stories, crime reports, and features that appealed to a wider
  • audience.

questions.question: Examine the role of Rev. Benjamin Bailey in the establishment of the printing press in Kerala.
questions.solution_html:
• Rev. Benjamin Bailey played a foundational role in establishing modern printing in Kerala,
  • particularly through his pioneering efforts in Kottayam during the early 19th century.
  • Benjamin Bailey established one of the earliest printing presses in Kerala in 1821 at CMS
  • Press under the auspices of the Church Missionary Society . Bailey was instrumental in
  • designing and casting the first Malayalam movable types. Bailey’s press laid the foundation
  • for later developments in Malayalam journalism and publishing.

questions.question: Assess the impact of early periodicals on literacy and education in Kochi.

• The early periodicals published in and around Kochi played a crucial role in shaping literacy
  • and education during the 19th and early 20th centuries. By pro moting reading habits,
  • simplifying language, supporting formal education, and spreading modern knowledge, they
  • significantly enhanced literacy and laid the foundation for Kerala’s later achievements in
  • education.
